# Kronos Fusion Energy — Learn — knowledge base

> Kronos Fusion Energy is a family-owned American fusion company: a D–T spherical-tokamak breeder (HYPERION) that makes tritium and helium-3, and a low-neutron D–³He tandem-mirror burner (Aegis / MetroVolt). This file lists the pages of the /learn section for AI crawlers and assistants. Public physics is open; economics are not published.

## Pages
- [Learn — Knowledge Base](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn): Open knowledge base on compact, low-neutron fusion: physics, engineering, economics, and the open questions behind the two Kronos machines — the HYPERION breeder and the tandem-mirror burner.
- [Aegis](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/aegis): Aegis is the compact, fixed-site housing of the Kronos D–³He tandem-mirror burner — a 440 m machine for defense and forward installations, delivering about +850 MWe net. Fixed-site, not shipboard.
- [Alfvén Eigenmodes (TAEs)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/alfven-eigenmodes): Fast fusion ions can excite Alfvén-wave instabilities that expel them before they heat the plasma. Kronos flags TAE transport as a named open channel.
- [Aspect Ratio](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/aspect-ratio): Aspect ratio is the ratio of a tokamak
- [Balance of Plant](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/balance-of-plant): Balance of plant is everything outside the reactor core — cooling, power conditioning, controls. Direct energy conversion shrinks it versus a steam plant.
- [Ballooning &amp; Mercier Stability](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/ballooning-mercier): Ballooning and Mercier modes are pressure-driven instabilities that cap how much pressure a plasma can hold. Kronos checks its second-stability access.
- [Baseload vs Dispatchable Power](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/baseload-vs-dispatchable-power): Baseload runs steadily; dispatchable follows demand. A fusion plant can do both — firm baseload that also modulates to help balance the grid.
- [Biological Shielding &amp; Site Safety](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/biological-shielding): Biological shielding protects workers and the public from radiation during operation. A low-neutron plant needs less of it and poses no evacuation-scale risk.
- [Bootstrap Fraction](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/bootstrap-fraction): The bootstrap fraction (f_BS) is the share of plasma current the plasma drives itself — reducing the external current-drive power a fusion plant must pay for.
- [Bremsstrahlung Radiation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/bremsstrahlung): Bremsstrahlung is
- [Can a fusion plant follow demand?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-a-fusion-plant-follow-demand): A fusion plant is firm and dispatchable — ideal for steady base load, and able to adjust output to help balance the grid.
- [Can a fusion reactor explode or melt down?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-a-fusion-reactor-melt-down): No. Fusion has no chain reaction and holds only seconds of fuel — any interruption stops the reaction. There is no meltdown or explosion pathway.
- [Can fusion energy be used to make weapons?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-be-used-for-weapons): A fusion power plant produces no weapons-usable material — no plutonium, no enriched uranium. Low-neutron D–³He minimizes even the indirect proliferation concern.
- [Can fusion make hydrogen or industrial heat?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-make-hydrogen-or-industrial-heat): Yes. Firm, DC-native fusion electricity is well suited to hydrogen electrolysis, and a fusion plant can supply high-grade industrial heat as well as power.
- [Can Fusion Power a Data Center?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-power-a-data-center): A full-length MetroVolt burner delivers roughly +2832 MWe of firm, continuous power — matched to hyperscale data-center campuses that need clean baseload independent of grid congestion.
- [Can fusion power ships or spacecraft?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-power-ships-or-spacecraft): Fusion
- [Can Fusion Provide Firm, Baseload Power?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-provide-baseload-power): Yes — firm baseload is exactly what the Kronos machines are built for. Both run steady-state, delivering continuous output rather than the intermittent profile of wind and solar.
- [Can fusion really work on Earth?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-really-work-on-earth): Yes — fusion has been achieved many times in labs. The challenge isn
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-fusion-scale-fast-enough-for-climate)
- [Can I see the data behind Kronos's claims?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/can-i-see-the-data-behind-kronos): Yes. Kronos deposits its full 81-analysis simulation record — code and data — openly under CC BY 4.0 at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21746157.
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/capacity-factor)
- [Dr. Carl Weggel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/carl-weggel): Dr. Carl Weggel is Kronos
- [The Carnot Limit](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/carnot-limit): The Carnot limit caps the efficiency of any heat engine. Direct energy conversion sidesteps it entirely — the efficiency case for the Kronos approach.
- [Catalyzed D–D Fuel Cycle](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/catalyzed-d-d): In a catalyzed D–D cycle, deuterium fuses with itself and the products (³He and tritium) are burned in turn — how Kronos breeds its own helium-3.
- [The Central Solenoid](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/central-solenoid): The central solenoid is the transformer coil that ramps the plasma current at startup. Its flux demand sets part of the machine
- [Charged-Particle Direct Converter (CPDC)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/charged-particle-direct-converter): A CPDC decelerates charged fusion products against an electric field, recovering their energy directly as electricity — a core mode of the Kronos DEC train.
- [Compact vs Conventional Fusion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/compact-vs-conventional-fusion): Compact high-field machines reach reactor conditions in a fraction of the size of conventional low-field designs — cheaper, faster, and manufacturable as a product.
- [Confinement Scaling Laws (IPB98)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/confinement-scaling-laws): Because confinement can
- [Copper vs Superconducting Magnets](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/copper-vs-superconducting-magnets): Copper magnets waste enormous power as heat and can
- [Cryogenics &amp; Magnet Cooling](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/cryogenics): Superconducting magnets must be kept cold. HTS lets Kronos run near 20 K rather than 4 K — a meaningful engineering and efficiency easing.
- [Current Drive &amp; Non-Inductive Operation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/current-drive): Current drive sustains the plasma current without a transformer, enabling steady-state operation. Kronos runs a high non-inductive fraction.
- [Deep Dive: Current Drive &amp; Bootstrap](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/current-drive-and-bootstrap-deep-dive): Steady-state operation needs the plasma to supply most of its own current. Kronos reaches a bootstrap fraction of 0.59–0.78, topped up by non-inductive drive.
- [D–³He vs D–D](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/d-he3-vs-d-d): D–D is the reaction that breeds Kronos
- [D–³He vs D–T Fuel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/d-he3-vs-d-t): Deuterium–helium-3 versus deuterium–tritium: fewer neutrons, direct energy conversion, and a harder ignition problem. A side-by-side for the Kronos choice.
- [D–³He vs p–¹¹B Fuel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/d-he3-vs-p-11b): Both are advanced low-neutron fuels. D–³He is the achievable commercial baseline; p–¹¹B is truly aneutronic but harder — the gated endpoint of the Kronos roadmap.
- [DC-Native vs AC Output](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/dc-native-vs-ac-output): Direct energy conversion gives Kronos a DC-native output, unlike the AC from a turbine-generator. That
- [Demountable Magnets](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/demountable-magnets): Demountable joints let a fusion magnet be opened for maintenance and assembly — a practical advantage of REBCO that Kronos builds into its winding pack.
- [Deuterium](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/deuterium): Deuterium is a heavy, stable isotope of hydrogen abundant in seawater — one half of the Kronos staged D–³He fuel cycle.
- [Deuterium vs Tritium](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/deuterium-vs-tritium): Deuterium is stable, abundant, and from seawater; tritium is radioactive, scarce, and must be bred. Kronos runs mostly deuterium with only a minimal tritium role.
- [Direct Conversion vs the Steam Cycle](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/direct-conversion-vs-steam-cycle): Direct energy conversion turns charged particles straight into electricity; a steam cycle boils water for a turbine. DEC skips the Carnot limit and shrinks the plant.
- [Direct Energy Conversion (DEC)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/direct-energy-conversion): Direct energy conversion turns the charged particles leaving a plasma straight into electricity, skipping the steam cycle. In the Kronos burner, the tandem mirror
- [Direct Internal Recovery (DIR)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/direct-internal-recovery): DIR recovers and recycles unburned fuel within the plant on a single pass. Kronos targets &gt;95% single-pass extraction — pre-registered prediction P4.
- [Displacements Per Atom (dpa)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/displacements-per-atom): dpa measures neutron damage to materials — how many times each atom is knocked from its lattice site. Kronos
- [Disruptions & Safety, In Depth](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/disruptions-and-safety-deep-dive): A deeper look at how the two Kronos machines differ on disruption safety: the breeder manages tokamak disruptions conservatively, while the tandem-mirror burner removes the disruption failure mode by architecture.
- [Does D–³He fusion produce neutrons?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/does-d-he3-produce-neutrons): The primary D–³He reaction is aneutronic, but side D–D reactions make some neutrons — which is why Kronos says
- [Does fusion produce any CO₂?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/does-fusion-produce-co2): A fusion plant emits no CO₂ while generating power. The only carbon is the one-time embodied emissions of construction, as with any power plant.
- [Does fusion produce radioactive waste?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/does-fusion-produce-radioactive-waste): Fusion produces no long-lived spent fuel — only activated structures that decay to recyclable levels in about a century. A low-neutron plant produces even less.
- [Does fusion use lasers?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/does-fusion-use-lasers): Some fusion does — inertial confinement uses lasers to compress fuel. Kronos uses magnetic confinement instead, holding the plasma in a magnetic field.
- [Does Kronos Depend on a Breakthrough?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/does-kronos-depend-on-a-breakthrough): Kronos
- [Edge-Localized Modes (ELMs)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/edge-localized-modes): ELMs are violent edge instabilities that can destroy plasma-facing hardware. Kronos avoids them entirely with an ELM-free negative-triangularity edge.
- [Effective Charge (Z_eff) &amp; Plasma Purity](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/effective-charge-zeff): Z_eff measures how much impurity contaminates a plasma. Keeping it low protects fusion rate and limits radiation — a constant operational goal.
- [Electron Bernstein Wave (EBW) Heating](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/electron-bernstein-wave): EBW heating reaches the dense core of a spherical tokamak where ordinary microwaves can
- [Elongation (κ)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/elongation): Elongation stretches the plasma cross-section vertically for higher current and pressure. Kronos runs a strongly shaped κ = 2.56.
- [Energy Confinement Time (τ_E)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/energy-confinement-time): τ_E measures how long a plasma holds its heat. Confinement scalings and the required H98 = 2.28 multiplier are expressed against it.
- [Energy Return on Investment (EROI)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/energy-return-on-investment): EROI is the ratio of energy a plant delivers over its life to the energy invested to build and run it — a measure fusion aims to score highly on.
- [Engineering Gain (Q_E)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/engineering-gain): Engineering gain, Q_E, is the ratio of net electricity out to electricity in — the number that actually matters for a power plant. The Kronos burner
- [Error Fields &amp; Correction](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/error-fields): Tiny imperfections in the magnets create error fields that can lock modes and trigger disruptions. Correction coils cancel them.
- [Fast-Ion Channeling (P6)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fast-ion-channeling): Fast-ion channeling redirects energetic-ion energy into the plasma fuel ions — a key Kronos upside, bounded and gated as prediction P6.
- [Firm Clean Power Options Compared](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/firm-clean-power-options-compared): Fusion, fission, geothermal, hydro, and gas-with-capture all offer firm low-carbon power. Here
- [Firm Fusion Power for Data Centers](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/firm-power-for-data-centers): MetroVolt targets the hardest energy problem in computing: firm, clean, gigawatt-scale power sited next to hyperscale campuses, delivered continuously through direct conversion and a thermal cycle.
- [Firm vs Intermittent Power](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/firm-vs-intermittent-power): Firm power is available on demand; intermittent power depends on weather. Understanding the difference explains why a clean grid needs both — and where fusion fits.
- [Flux Surfaces &amp; the Separatrix](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/flux-surfaces): Nested magnetic flux surfaces confine the plasma; the separatrix is the last closed one. Together they define where the plasma ends and exhaust begins.
- [Fuel Abundance &amp; Energy Security](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fuel-abundance-energy-security): Kronos
- [The Fuel Strategy: Breed, Then Burn](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fuel-staging): Kronos

- [Fusion &amp; the Electrification of Everything](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-and-electrification): Electrifying transport, heat, and industry will multiply electricity demand — and much of that new demand needs to be firm and clean. That
- [Fusion Cross-Section &amp; Reactivity](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-cross-section): The cross-section measures how likely two nuclei are to fuse at a given energy. D–³He peaks at higher temperature than D–T — shaping the Kronos operating point.
- [Fusion for Controlled-Environment Agriculture](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-agriculture): Indoor and vertical farming need firm, cheap power (and heat, and CO₂) to grow food anywhere. Firm fusion could make local, resilient food production viable.
- [Fusion for AI Compute](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-ai-compute): AI compute is becoming an energy problem. Kronos
- [Fusion for Arctic &amp; Extreme Environments](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-arctic-and-extreme-environments): Remote cold-climate operations depend on costly airlifted diesel. A firm, islandable fusion generator could power them cleanly and independently.
- [Fusion for Campuses &amp; Microgrids](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-campuses-and-microgrids): Universities, hospitals, and industrial campuses increasingly run their own microgrids for reliability. A firm fusion generator could anchor them with clean, resilient power.

- [Fusion for Defense Installations](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-defense-installations): Aegis is the Kronos burner sized for fixed defense and forward installations: firm, self-contained power delivered by rail and assembled on site, independent of fuel convoys and vulnerable grid ties.
- [Fusion for Desalination](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-desalination): Water-scarce regions need firm power (and sometimes heat) to desalinate at scale. A firm, low-water, siteable fusion plant is well matched to coastal desalination.
- [Fusion for Developing Economies](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-developing-economies): Firm clean power without fuel imports could let fast-growing economies electrify and industrialize cleanly — energy independence from a compact, siteable source.
- [Fusion for Direct Air Capture](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-direct-air-capture): Pulling CO₂ from the air is enormously energy-intensive and only makes sense with cheap, firm, clean power — a natural application for firm fusion.
- [Fusion for Disaster Response](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-disaster-response): After disasters, grids fail and fuel runs short. A firm, islandable fusion generator could keep critical power flowing when it
- [Fusion for District Cooling](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-district-cooling): Hot-climate cities increasingly run district cooling networks that demand large, steady power. Firm fusion could supply that cooling load cleanly and reliably.
- [Fusion for District Heating](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-district-heating): City heating networks need firm, low-carbon heat. A fusion plant can supply both power and heat to a district system — with siting flexibility to sit near the city.
- [Fusion for EV Charging Networks](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-ev-charging): Fast-charging hubs draw large, spiky DC loads that strain grids. Firm, DC-native fusion power is a natural anchor for high-throughput EV charging.
- [Fusion for Green Ammonia](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-green-ammonia): Ammonia is vital for fertilizer and a promising clean fuel, but its production is fossil-fired today. Firm fusion power could make green ammonia — securing food and a fuel at once.
- [Fusion for Green Hydrogen](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-green-hydrogen): Firm, DC-native fusion power is an ideal match for hydrogen electrolysis — high utilization and a direct DC feed make for cheaper, cleaner hydrogen.
- [Fusion for Grid Resilience](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-grid-resilience): Firm, islandable, inertia-providing generation makes a grid resilient to outages and extreme weather. A fusion plant delivers all three.
- [Fusion for Heavy Industry](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-heavy-industry): Steel, cement, and chemicals need vast firm heat and power — among the hardest emissions to abate. Firm fusion, co-locating clean heat and electricity, is a route to decarbonizing them.

- [Fusion for Industrial Process Heat](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-industrial-heat): Industry needs vast firm heat, much of it fossil-fired today. A fusion plant can supply firm high-grade heat and power together — a route to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify industry.
- [Fusion for Island Nations](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-island-nations): Islands often depend on costly, imported diesel for power. A firm, islandable fusion generator could give them clean, self-sufficient energy independence.
- [Fusion for Metals &amp; Smelting](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-metals-and-smelting): Producing aluminum, steel, and other metals is enormously electricity-intensive. Firm clean fusion power could decarbonize electrometallurgy without sacrificing reliability.
- [Fusion for Mining](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-mining): Mines are often remote, diesel-dependent, and electrifying fast. Firm, islandable fusion power could replace diesel and run electric mining fleets cleanly.
- [Fusion for Ports &amp; Logistics Hubs](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-ports-and-logistics): Ports are electrifying — shore power for ships, electric cranes and trucks — creating large firm loads. Firm fusion power could anchor a zero-carbon port.
- [Fusion for Remote Microgrids](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-remote-microgrids): Remote and islanded sites depend on fuel convoys and diesel. A firm, islandable fusion generator gives them clean, self-sufficient power without a supply line.
- [Fusion for Shipping](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-shipping): Shipping is hard to decarbonize because fuel energy density matters at sea. Fusion
- [Fusion for Space Habitats](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-space-habitats): Off-world bases will need compact, firm, fuel-light power far from resupply. Low-neutron fusion is a compelling long-horizon candidate — though not Kronos
- [Fusion for Space Propulsion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-space-propulsion): Fusion
- [Fusion for Synthetic Fuels](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-synthetic-fuels): Synthetic e-fuels need vast firm clean electricity to be viable. Firm, DC-native fusion power at high utilization is a strong match for producing them.
- [Fusion for Water Treatment](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-for-water-treatment): Desalination and advanced water treatment are energy-intensive. Firm, low-water fusion power could secure fresh water for arid and growing regions.
- [Fusion Fuel vs Fission Fuel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-fuel-vs-fission-fuel): Fusion runs on hydrogen isotopes from seawater with no enrichment or proliferation risk; fission runs on mined, enriched uranium with spent-fuel and safeguards burdens.
- [Fusion Gain (Q)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-gain-q): Q is the ratio of fusion power produced to heating power supplied. Kronos is honest that its endpoint is a driven system, not an igniting one.
- [The Fuel 'Generations' — and Where Kronos Sits](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-generations): Fusion fuels form a cleanliness ladder from D–T to D–³He to aneutronic p–¹¹B. Kronos runs the first two — D–T in the breeder, low-neutron D–³He in the burner. p–¹¹B is an industry-wide ideal, not a Kronos endpoint.
- [Fusion Neutronics](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-neutronics): Neutronics is the study of how fusion neutrons travel, deposit energy, and activate materials. For a low-neutron plant, the numbers are far gentler.
- [Fusion Power Density](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-power-density): Fusion power density rises steeply with magnetic field and pressure — the physics that lets a high-field compact tokamak rival a much larger one.
- [Fusion vs Antimatter](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-antimatter): Antimatter has the highest energy density imaginable — but can
- [Fusion vs Battery Storage](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-battery-storage): Batteries shift energy across hours; fusion generates firm energy continuously. They solve different problems — and storage can
- [Fusion vs Coal](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-coal): Both are firm, always-on power — but coal emits CO₂ and pollution and depends on mining, while fusion is clean and runs on seawater-derived fuel.
- [Fusion vs Enhanced Geothermal](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-enhanced-geothermal): Enhanced geothermal drills deep to reach heat anywhere, but faces geology and seismicity limits. Fusion delivers firm clean power without drilling or induced-seismicity risk.
- [Fusion vs Fission Safety](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-fission-safety): Fission needs active safety systems to manage a chain reaction and decay heat; fusion fails safe by physics — no runaway, no meltdown, no evacuation zone.
- [Fusion vs Geothermal](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-geothermal): Both are firm, clean, always-on power — but geothermal is limited to favorable geology, while a compact fusion plant can be sited near the load it serves.
- [Fusion vs Hydropower](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-hydropower): Hydropower is firm, clean, and dispatchable — but geographically limited and largely built out. Fusion offers the same firm clean profile without the geography constraint.
- [Fusion vs Natural Gas](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-natural-gas): Gas is firm and flexible but emits CO₂ and methane and rides volatile fuel markets. Fusion offers the same firmness and flexibility with zero operating emissions and stable fuel.
- [Fusion vs Small Modular Reactors](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-small-modular-reactors): Both aim at firm, modular clean power — but SMRs are fission (spent fuel, proliferation, mined fuel) while fusion has no chain reaction and no long-lived waste.
- [Fusion vs Solar](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-solar): Solar is the cheapest energy ever built — but intermittent and land-hungry. Fusion is firm and compact. The clean grid needs both, in different roles.
- [Fusion vs Space-Based Solar](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-space-based-solar): Space-based solar beams power from orbit — clean and near-constant, but staggeringly complex and costly. Terrestrial fusion offers firm clean power without leaving Earth.
- [Fusion vs Wind](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-vs-wind): Wind is cheap but intermittent and land-hungry; fusion is firm and compact. They
- [Fusion Waste &amp; Decommissioning](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/fusion-waste): Fusion produces no long-lived spent fuel — only activated structures that decay to recyclable levels. A low-neutron plant produces even less.
- [Dr. Gerald Kulcinski](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/gerald-kulcinski): Dr. Gerald Kulcinski is a founding partner of Kronos, an advanced-fuel and helium-3 fusion specialist whose expertise anchors the low-neutron D–³He fuel strategy.
- [The Graded Winding Pack](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/graded-winding-pack): Kronos grades its magnet winding pack layer by layer to the local field, keeping strain within margin at the operating peak while staying demountable.
- [The Greenwald Density Limit](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/greenwald-limit): The Greenwald limit is an empirical ceiling on tokamak plasma density. Negative-triangularity operation lets Kronos run above the conventional fraction.
- [Grid Firming & Dispatchable Power](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/grid-firming): Grid firming means supplying power that is available on demand, smoothing the variability of wind and solar. Kronos
- [Grid Inertia &amp; Stability Services](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/grid-inertia): Grids need inertia and stability services that intermittent renewables don
- [Gyrokinetic Turbulence](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/gyrokinetic-turbulence): Gyrokinetics models the small-scale turbulence that drains heat from a plasma. The nonlinear gyrokinetic check on Kronos confinement is the outstanding verification.
- [Gyroradius &amp; ρ*](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/gyroradius): Charged particles spiral with a gyroradius set by field and temperature. Its normalized value ρ* governs how experiments scale to a reactor.
- [H-mode and L-mode](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/h-mode-and-l-mode): H-mode is a high-confinement regime with a dangerous edge; L-mode is quieter but leakier. Kronos uses negative triangularity to get the best of both.
- [Hafnium Carbide First Wall](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/hafnium-carbide-wall): Kronos uses a laser-fused hafnium carbide first wall — a refractory, highly reflective surface that recycles synchrotron radiation.
- [Has anyone achieved net-energy fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/has-anyone-achieved-net-energy-fusion): At the reaction level, yes — the 2022 NIF experiment released more fusion energy than the laser delivered to the target. Plant-level net energy, counting all inputs, has not yet been demonstrated.
- [Has Kronos Built a Reactor Yet?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/has-kronos-built-a-reactor-yet): No. Kronos is at the design and validation stage: two papers, two open deposits, and a live simulation. The next physical step is a confinement testbed, not a power plant.
- [Helium-3](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/helium-3): Helium-3 is a rare, light helium isotope and the second half of Kronos
- [Helium-3: Terrestrial vs Lunar](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/helium-3-terrestrial-vs-lunar): Earth
- [Helium Ash &amp; Exhaust](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/helium-ash): Fusion produces helium
- [High-Harmonic Fast Wave (HHFW)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/high-harmonic-fast-wave): HHFW is a radio-frequency method for heating and driving current in spherical tokamaks — and the launcher Kronos proposes for the fast-ion channeling test.
- [High-Temperature Superconductivity](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/high-temperature-superconductivity): HTS materials carry lossless current at high field and warmer temperatures than old superconductors — the breakthrough enabling compact high-field fusion.
- [High vs Low Aspect Ratio](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/high-vs-low-aspect-ratio): Low aspect ratio (spherical) raises beta and stability but crowds the center stack; high aspect ratio is roomier but lower-performance. Kronos runs a low A = 2.0.
- [Hot-Ion Mode](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/hot-ion-mode): Hot-ion mode runs the fuel ions hotter than the electrons, boosting fusion output while limiting radiation losses. Both Kronos machines rely on it — the breeder for gain, the burner at ~90 keV ion temperature.
- [How can I partner with Kronos?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-can-i-partner-with-kronos): Kronos works through strategic partnerships — offtake, siting, technology, and defense collaboration. The contact page is the front door.
- [How Do MetroVolt and Aegis Differ?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-do-metrovolt-and-aegis-differ): They are the same D–³He tandem-mirror burner at two lengths: Aegis (~440 m, +850 MWe) for fixed defense installations, and MetroVolt (~1400 m, +2832 MWe) for cities and data centers.
- [How do you confine something that hot?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-do-you-confine-a-plasma): You don
- [How does a tokamak work?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-a-tokamak-work): A tokamak confines fusion plasma in a magnetic bottle shaped like a doughnut, using a combination of external coils and a current in the plasma itself.
- [How is fusion different from nuclear fission?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-fusion-differ-from-fission): Fusion joins light nuclei; fission splits heavy ones. Fusion has no chain reaction, cannot melt down, and leaves no long-lived waste.
- [How does a fusion plant actually make electricity?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-fusion-make-electricity): Most fusion concepts boil water for a steam turbine. Kronos captures charged-particle energy directly as electricity, skipping the steam cycle entirely.
- [How does Kronos's business work?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-kronos-business-work): Kronos develops fusion generators and plans to earn revenue through power offtake, plant sales, and strategic and defense partnerships — publishing its work to build trust with those partners.
- [How Does Kronos Compare to ITER?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-kronos-compare-to-iter): The Kronos breeder is far more compact than ITER: a 1.2 m major radius versus 6.2 m, and a plasma current of 9.66 MA — about two-thirds of ITER
- [How Does Kronos Handle Disruptions?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-kronos-handle-disruptions): The Kronos breeder handles disruptions the way modern tokamaks do — detection plus mitigation — while running a conservative stability margin. The tandem-mirror burner avoids disruptions entirely, by having no plasma cur
- [How does Kronos validate its simulations?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-kronos-validate-its-simulations): Through a three-tier evidence discipline — reduced-order engines, deposited input decks, and referee-defense analyses — cross-validated and released openly as 81 analyses.
- [How Does MetroVolt Connect to the Grid?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-metrovolt-connect-to-the-grid): MetroVolt delivers firm, dispatchable baseload — roughly +2832 MWe — through direct energy conversion and standard high-voltage transmission, siting near the large continuous loads it serves.
- [How does the reactor survive the heat?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-does-the-reactor-survive-the-heat): The plasma core never touches the wall. The wall handles a manageable edge flux, exhaust goes to the divertor, and low-neutron fuel limits material damage.
- [How hot is a fusion plasma?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-hot-is-a-fusion-plasma): A fusion plasma runs at over 100 million degrees — hotter than the sun
- [How is AI used in a fusion plant?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-is-ai-used-in-a-fusion-plant): Kronos designs an AI-native control stack — a real-time digital twin, anomaly detection, and deterministic safety clamps — to hold the plasma within its envelope faster than a human could.
- [How long does a fusion plant last?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-long-does-a-fusion-plant-last): Kronos designs MetroVolt on a 30 full-power-year basis, and its low-neutron first wall lasts that full life without replacement.
- [How long have we been researching fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-long-have-we-researched-fusion): Since the 1950s — about seven decades of steady progress, recently accelerated by high-temperature superconductors, private investment, and the 2022 ignition milestone.
- [How many fusion plants would it take to matter?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-many-fusion-plants-would-we-need): Global electricity demand is measured in terawatts, so meaningful fusion deployment means thousands of gigawatt-scale units — which is why manufacturability is everything.
- [How Much Electricity Does One MetroVolt Produce?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-much-electricity-does-one-metrovolt-produce): A MetroVolt, the long form of the Kronos burner at about 1400 m, delivers roughly +2832 MWe net at the frozen closing point — because the tandem mirror
- [How much land does a fusion plant need?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-much-land-does-a-fusion-plant-need): A fusion plant is compact for its output — high power density means a small footprint compared with the land solar or wind needs for equivalent firm energy.
- [How precisely must the plasma be controlled?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-precisely-must-the-plasma-be-controlled): Extremely — position, shape, and stability must be held on millisecond and microsecond timescales, which is why Kronos designs an automated, twin-assisted control stack.
- [How Strong Are the Kronos Fields?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/how-strong-is-a-24-tesla-magnet): Very strong: Kronos uses compact HTS coils in the breeder and a 26.49 T end-plug throat in the burner — many times Earth
- [HTS vs LTS Magnets](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/hts-vs-lts-magnets): High-temperature superconductors reach far higher fields and warmer temperatures than low-temperature ones — the difference that makes compact high-field fusion possible.
- [Ignition vs Driven Operation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/ignition-vs-driven): An igniting plasma sustains itself; a driven one needs continuous heating. Kronos designs to a driven operating point and says so plainly.
- [Impurity Seeding &amp; the Radiative Divertor](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/impurity-seeding): Deliberately adding trace impurities makes the exhaust radiate its heat away before it reaches the target — how Kronos achieves divertor detachment.
- [Inertial Confinement Fusion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/inertial-confinement-fusion): Inertial confinement compresses a fuel pellet with lasers for a brief burst — the main alternative to the magnetic approach Kronos uses.
- [Ion &amp; Electron Temperature](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/ion-and-electron-temperature): Fusion depends on the ion temperature; the electrons are where losses concentrate. The ratified Mode-D baseline is near-thermal (Ti = Te); the hot-ion posture is a gated, labeled-history ceiling.

- [Is fusion energy clean and renewable?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-fusion-energy-clean): Fusion emits no CO₂, produces no long-lived waste, and runs on effectively inexhaustible fuel — clean by any measure, and effectively renewable.
- [Is fusion energy like a hydrogen bomb?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-fusion-energy-like-a-hydrogen-bomb): No. Both involve fusion, but a power plant holds only seconds of fuel in a controlled plasma that can
- [Is fusion power safe?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-fusion-power-safe): Fusion cannot melt down or run away, and a low-neutron design minimizes activation and long-lived waste. Here is the honest safety picture for the Kronos design.
- [Is fusion safe for the people who work there?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-fusion-safe-for-workers): Yes. The hazards — magnet energy, tritium, activated components — are engineering-controlled with standard radiation-protection practice, and there
- [Is helium-3 really mined on the moon?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-helium-3-really-mined-on-the-moon): Lunar regolith genuinely holds helium-3, and it
- [Is it safe to build fusion near cities?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-it-safe-to-build-fusion-near-cities): Yes. Fusion has no runaway-accident pathway and no evacuation zone, and a compact, low-water, low-neutron plant is well suited to siting near the loads it serves.
- [Is Kronos Fusion Aneutronic?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-kronos-fusion-aneutronic): No. Kronos is low-neutron, not aneutronic. The breeder burns neutron-rich D–T on purpose to breed fuel; the burner runs D–³He at a ~5.44% neutron fraction — small and adjustable, but not zero.
- [Is tritium dangerous?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/is-tritium-dangerous): Tritium is radioactive but emits only weak radiation and is managed routinely in industry. Kronos
- [Isn't fusion always 30 years away?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/isnt-fusion-always-30-years-away): That reputation came from decades of underfunding and overpromising. Kronos avoids date-promises entirely, advancing through pre-registered gates with published results.
- [Ion-Temperature-Gradient (ITG) Turbulence](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/itg-turbulence): ITG modes are the dominant heat-loss turbulence in hot plasmas. Running the ions hotter than the electrons raises the ITG threshold — a key Kronos lever.
- [The Kink Instability](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/kink-instability): The kink is a current-driven instability that can disrupt a tokamak. A safety factor above ~2 (Kronos holds q95 ≥ 5) keeps it at bay.
- [The Lawson Criterion &amp; Triple Product](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/lawson-criterion): The Lawson criterion sets the density-temperature-confinement product a plasma must reach to sustain net fusion. Here is how it frames the Kronos design.
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/levelized-cost-of-electricity)
- [Lithium-6 & the No-Breeding Claim](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/lithium-6-no-breeding-claim): Lithium-6 breeds tritium from fusion neutrons. The Kronos breeder uses that on purpose; the D–³He burner does not breed at all. The
- [Magnet Quench &amp; Protection](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/magnet-quench): A quench is when part of a superconducting magnet suddenly goes resistive, dumping huge stored energy. Protecting against it is critical magnet engineering.
- [Magnetic Confinement](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/magnetic-confinement): Magnetic confinement uses powerful fields to hold a fusion plasma away from any wall. It is the approach behind tokamaks like Kronos MetroVolt.
- [Magnetic Islands](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/magnetic-islands): Magnetic islands are chains of closed loops that break the smooth nesting of flux surfaces, short-circuiting confinement across them.
- [Magnetic vs Inertial Confinement](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/magnetic-vs-inertial-confinement): Magnetic confinement holds a steady plasma in a field; inertial confinement compresses fuel pellets with lasers in pulses. Kronos is magnetic — suited to continuous power.
- [MetroVolt](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/metrovolt): MetroVolt is the long-form housing of the Kronos D–³He tandem-mirror burner — a 1400 m machine for cities and data centers, delivering about +2832 MWe net at the frozen closing point.
- [Plasma-Exhaust MHD Generator](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/mhd-generator): An MHD generator extracts electricity from flowing conducting plasma exhaust with no moving parts — one mode of the Kronos multi-modal converter.
- [Deep Dive: MHD Stability](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/mhd-stability-deep-dive): A survey of the stability limits Kronos must respect — kink, ballooning, vertical, and resistive-wall modes — and how the design stays inside them at β_N = 4.96.
- [Negative Triangularity](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/negative-triangularity): Negative triangularity (δ = −0.30) shapes the plasma cross-section to suppress edge instabilities — the design invariant at the core of the Kronos MetroVolt architecture.
- [Negative vs Positive Triangularity](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/negative-vs-positive-triangularity): Positive triangularity buys easy H-mode access with dangerous ELMs; negative triangularity trades that for an ELM-free edge. Why Kronos picked the reverse shape.
- [Neoclassical Tearing Modes (NTMs)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/neoclassical-tearing-modes): NTMs are magnetic islands seeded by the bootstrap current that degrade confinement. They are controllable with localized current drive.
- [Neoclassical Transport](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/neoclassical-transport): Neoclassical transport is the irreducible collisional leakage from a torus
- [Neutral Beam Injection (NBI)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/neutral-beam-injection): NBI fires fast neutral atoms into the plasma to heat it, drive current, and set rotation — a workhorse tool with multiple roles in the Kronos design.
- [Neutron Activation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/neutron-activation): Neutron activation is how fusion neutrons make structures mildly radioactive. A low-neutron design minimizes it — Kronos
- [Which Kronos Machine Needs a Breeding Blanket?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/no-breeding-blanket): The Kronos burner needs no breeding blanket — its D–³He fuel is supplied, not bred. The breeder deliberately has one: breeding tritium is its whole job. The claim applies to the burner, not the breeder.

- [Open Data &amp; Reproducibility](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/open-data-reproducibility): Kronos releases its full simulation record — 81 analyses, code and data — openly under CC BY 4.0, so anyone can check the numbers behind the design.
- [Pellet Fuelling](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/pellet-fuelling): Firing frozen fuel pellets deep into the plasma core keeps the density and reaction rate up — the main core-fuelling method for a reactor.
- [Photonic Energy Capture](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/photonic-energy-capture): Photonic capture recovers energy from the radiation a plasma emits — bremsstrahlung and synchrotron light — as another stage of the Kronos converter.
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plant-lifetime)
- [Plasma Beta (β)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-beta): Beta measures how much plasma pressure a magnetic field holds — an efficiency and stability metric. Kronos runs β_N = 4.96 at the frozen Mode-D point, wall-stabilized against the computed 5.0 limit.
- [Plasma Current (I_p)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-current): Plasma current confines and heats a tokamak plasma. The Kronos breeder runs 9.66 MA — about two-thirds of ITER
- [Plasma Density &amp; Fuelling](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-density-and-fuelling): Fusion power rises with the square of density, so running dense is valuable. Kronos operates above the Greenwald limit, sustained by careful fuelling.
- [Plasma Diagnostics](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-diagnostics): Diagnostics are the sensors that measure a plasma in real time. Kronos
- [Plasma Disruption](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-disruption): A disruption is a sudden loss of tokamak plasma confinement, dumping current and energy into the wall. The Kronos breeder must manage them; the tandem-mirror burner cannot disrupt at all — it has no plasma current.
- [Plasma-Facing Components (PFCs)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-facing-components): PFCs are the materials that directly face the plasma — first wall and divertor. They must survive extreme heat, particles, and radiation.
- [Deep Dive: Plasma-Facing Materials](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-facing-materials-deep-dive): The first wall must survive heat, particle bombardment, and radiation for the plant
- [Plasma Heating](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-heating): Fusion plasmas must reach 100+ million degrees. External heating — neutral beams and radio-frequency waves — brings them there and drives current.
- [Plasma Rotation &amp; Flow Shear](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-rotation): A rotating plasma with sheared flow suppresses turbulence and helps stabilize instabilities — a lever that supports the Kronos confinement and stability case.
- [Plasma Startup &amp; the Ramp Phase](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/plasma-startup): Starting a tokamak means breaking down the gas, ramping the current, and heating to burn — a choreographed sequence Kronos budgets flux and power for.
- [Poloidal Field &amp; Shaping Coils](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/poloidal-field-coils): Poloidal field coils position and shape the plasma — setting its elongation, triangularity, and vertical stability. They hold the Kronos NT shape.
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/power-purchase-agreement)
- [Private vs Public Fusion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/private-vs-public-fusion): Public programs pursue fusion as large-scale science; private companies pursue it as a compact, manufacturable product. Kronos is private — and builds on decades of public research.
- [Proton–Boron-11 (p–¹¹B) Fusion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/proton-boron-11): p–¹¹B is the truly aneutronic fusion reaction — the gated research endpoint of the Kronos fuel roadmap, not its commercial baseline.
- [REBCO High-Temperature Superconducting Magnets](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/rebco-hts-magnets): REBCO high-temperature superconductors carry enormous current at high field, enabling compact fusion. Kronos uses them for the breeder
- [Remote Maintenance](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/remote-maintenance): Activated reactor components must be serviced remotely. A low-neutron design with demountable magnets makes maintenance faster and cheaper for Kronos.
- [Resistive Wall Mode (RWM)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/resistive-wall-mode): The RWM is a slow-growing instability at high beta that the conducting wall only partly suppresses. Kronos holds it with active feedback.
- [Dr. Robert J. Weggel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/robert-weggel): Dr. Robert J. Weggel leads magnetic-field design for Kronos, bringing MIT Magnet Lab high-field-magnet expertise to the 24.42 T REBCO magnet system.
- [Runaway Electrons](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/runaway-electrons): Runaway electrons are a tokamak disruption hazard: electrons accelerated to high energy that can damage the wall. The Kronos breeder must mitigate them; the tandem-mirror burner, having no current, cannot generate them t
- [Safety Factor (q₉₅)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/safety-factor-q95): The safety factor q₉₅ measures how tightly field lines wind around a tokamak — a key stability margin. The Kronos breeder holds q₉₅ above a ~5 floor at 9.66 MA. The tandem-mirror burner has no q₉₅.
- [The Sawtooth Instability](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/sawtooth-instability): Sawteeth are periodic, benign relaxations of the plasma core that flatten the central profiles. They are a managed feature, not a threat, in tokamak operation.
- [Deep Dive: Scientific Oversight &amp; Independent Audit](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/scientific-oversight-deep-dive): The MetroVolt design was stress-tested under an independent structure — founding partners, scientific advisors, and independent auditors — with a three-tier evidence discipline.
- [Scrape-Off Layer (SOL)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/scrape-off-layer): The SOL is the thin plasma layer beyond the last closed flux surface that carries exhaust to the divertor. Kronos widens it with Super-X geometry.
- [The Two-Machine Architecture](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/smart-architecture): Kronos is built around two machines with one job each: a spherical-tokamak D–T breeder (HYPERION) that makes the fuel, and a D–³He tandem-mirror burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) that burns it.
- [Spherical vs Conventional Tokamak](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/spherical-vs-conventional-tokamak): Low aspect ratio versus the classic thin donut: how the spherical tokamak trades a crowded center column for better stability and pressure efficiency.
- [Steady-State Operation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/steady-state-operation): A power plant must run continuously, not in pulses. Kronos reaches steady state with a high bootstrap fraction plus non-inductive current drive.
- [Steady-State vs Pulsed Operation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/steady-state-vs-pulsed-operation): A power plant should run continuously, not in pulses. Kronos targets steady-state operation via a high bootstrap fraction — avoiding the fatigue and downtime of pulsed machines.
- [Stellarator](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/stellarator): A stellarator confines plasma with twisted external coils and no plasma current — disruption-free but complex. Kronos chose the tokamak path.
- [The Super-X Divertor](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/super-x-divertor): A Super-X divertor lengthens and spreads the exhaust leg to ease heat load, enabling the detachment Kronos relies on. Its flux expansion is within demonstrated range.
- [Synchrotron Radiation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/synchrotron-radiation): Synchrotron radiation is emitted as electrons spiral in the magnetic field. At high field it matters — Kronos budgets 158 MW and relies on wall reflectivity.
- [The Kronos Magnet Systems](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-24-6-tesla-magnet-system): Kronos uses high field in two ways: compact HTS magnets in the spherical-tokamak breeder, and high-field end plugs in the tandem-mirror burner with a 26.49 T ion-end throat. The earlier 24.42 T tokamak magnet is supersed
- [Deep Dive: The AI-Native Plant](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-ai-native-plant-deep-dive): An eight-layer control architecture — from microsecond deterministic reflexes to a predictive digital twin and human oversight — that holds the plasma within its safety envelope.
- [The Center Stack](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-center-stack): The center stack is the crowded central column of a spherical tokamak, holding the inboard magnet and shield in minimal space — a low-neutron design
- [The Compact-Fusion Landscape](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-compact-fusion-landscape): A neutral map of the approaches in the field — high-field tokamaks, stellarators, FRCs, inertial and magneto-inertial — and where the Kronos design sits within it.
- [Deep Dive: The Confinement Case](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-confinement-case-deep-dive): The design needs H98 = 2.28, resting on negative triangularity and density headroom — anchored on DIII-D data, with the nonlinear gyrokinetic check outstanding.
- [Deep Dive: The Cryogenic System](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-cryogenic-system-deep-dive): The HTS magnets must be kept cold — but at ~20 K, not the ~4 K of low-temperature magnets. That higher operating temperature meaningfully eases the cryoplant.

- [Deep Dive: The Diagnostic Constellation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-diagnostic-constellation-deep-dive): A dense array of sensors measures the plasma thousands of times a second — magnetics, interferometry, spectroscopy, and structural gauges — feeding the real-time control stack.
- [The Digital Twin](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-digital-twin): A digital twin is a live, physics-based model running alongside the plant, predicting its state 50–100 ms ahead so the controller can act before events arrive.
- [The Divertor](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-divertor): The divertor is the plasma

- [Deep Dive: Fast-Ion Physics &amp; Channeling](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-fast-ion-physics-deep-dive): Energetic ions from fusion and heating must be confined, slowed usefully, and — ideally — channeled into the fuel. Kronos treats channeling as a bounded, gated upside.
- [Deep Dive: The Field-Lever Upgrade Path](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-field-lever-upgrade-deep-dive): The deposited S78 field-lever study mapped a constraint-checked B₀/R_c move; on 24 July 2026 the ratified Mode-D basis adopted the lever at the build limit — R_c = 1.50 m, B₀ = 6.37 T, 24.42 T peak.
- [The 2026 Paper Series](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-four-part-paper-series-deep-dive): Kronos
- [Deep Dive: Fuelling &amp; Exhaust](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-fuelling-and-exhaust-deep-dive): A burning plasma must be continuously fed and cleaned — fuel injected to the core, helium ash and unburned fuel pumped out and recycled at over 95% single-pass.
- [The Fusion Hardware Behind Kronos's Founders](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-fusion-hardware-behind-kronos): Kronos
- [Deep Dive: The Fusion Pilot Plant](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-fusion-pilot-plant-deep-dive): Between the physics testbed and the full commercial unit sits the Kronos FPP — a ~0.25 GW-class machine that proves integrated operation and can generate pilot revenue.
- [The Fusion Triple Product](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-fusion-triple-product): The triple product of density, temperature, and confinement time is the single figure of merit for how close a plasma is to net fusion.
- [What is the G1 confinement testbed?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-g1-testbed): G1 is a sub-scale spherical tokamak — the first Kronos gate — built to measure the design
- [The Gate Program](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-gate-program): Kronos plans a staged validation program: measure the load-bearing physics on a testbed before scaling. The first gate targets the breeder
- [The Gate Program, In Depth](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-gate-program-deep-dive): A closer look at the Kronos staged-validation logic: how each gate maps to a named requirement and a falsifiable claim, from the breeder
- [Deep Dive: The ³He Mass Balance](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-he3-mass-balance-deep-dive): How Kronos breeds and recycles helium-3 in a staged, catalyzed cycle — and the honest ~33% fleet self-sufficiency gap the analyses report.
- [Deep Dive: Heating &amp; Current-Drive Systems](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-heating-systems-deep-dive): Reaching 48 keV and sustaining current takes neutral beams and RF waves. In Kronos they do double duty — heating the plasma and driving non-inductive current.
- [Deep Dive: The Hot-Ion Posture](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-hot-ion-posture-deep-dive): Running the ions hotter than the electrons raises fusion output and limits losses — a real upside Kronos treats as a bet, with the near-thermal case as the operating baseline.
- [Deep Dive: Lawson &amp; the Triple Product](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-lawson-triple-product-deep-dive): The condition for net fusion — density × temperature × confinement time — done honestly with radiation losses, yielding the H98 = 2.28 requirement and a driven, not igniting, operating point.
- [Deep Dive: The Magnet &amp; Shield System](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-magnet-and-shield-system-deep-dive): Kronos
- [The Main Fusion Reactions](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-main-fusion-reactions): D–T, D–D, D–³He, and p–¹¹B are the fusion reactions that matter for power. Kronos
- [Deep Dive: The Multi-Modal DEC Train](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-multi-modal-dec-train-deep-dive): Kronos layers four conversion modes — direct charged-particle, MHD, thermionic, and photonic — to reach a blended, gate-adjudicated efficiency without betting on one method.
- [The Neutron Shield](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-neutron-shield): The shield stops fusion neutrons from damaging the magnet and activating the structure. A low-neutron plant needs far less of it — a compounding advantage.
- [Deep Dive: Neutronics &amp; Activation](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-neutronics-and-activation-deep-dive): How a low-neutron design transforms the shielding, material lifetime, and waste picture — with a high-fidelity OpenMC calculation planned to fix the numbers.
- [Deep Dive: The Open 81-Analysis Package](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-open-data-package-deep-dive): What
- [The Open Questions](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-open-questions-deep-dive): Kronos names its hardest unsolved problems: the breeder
- [Is p–¹¹B the Endpoint?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-p11b-endpoint-deep-dive): No longer. The Kronos burner fuel is low-neutron D–³He, not proton–boron-11. p–¹¹B remains an interesting aneutronic fuel to understand, but it is not a Kronos endpoint on the frozen roadmap.
- [The Plant Power Flow](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-plant-power-flow-deep-dive): How power flows through each Kronos machine: the breeder
- [The Plasma Pedestal](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-plasma-pedestal): The pedestal is the steep edge pressure barrier of H-mode — the thing that drives ELMs. Kronos
- [Deep Dive: Power Electronics &amp; Grid Interface](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-power-electronics-deep-dive): Direct energy conversion produces DC that power electronics condition — inverting to AC for the grid or feeding DC loads directly, and providing grid services.
- [Deep Dive: The Radial Build &amp; Center Stack](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-radial-build-deep-dive): Everything must fit across the machine
- [The Fuel Cycle, In Depth](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-staged-fuel-cycle-deep-dive): A deeper look at the Kronos breed-then-burn fuel cycle: how a D–T spherical tokamak breeds tritium and helium-3, and how that decay inventory seeds the D–³He tandem-mirror burner.
- [Deep Dive: Cold Start to Grid](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-startup-sequence-deep-dive): The sequence that takes a Kronos plant from cold vacuum to grid power — breakdown, current ramp, heating to burn, and handoff to steady-state operation.
- [Deep Dive: Tritium &amp; Fuel Processing](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-tritium-and-fuel-processing-deep-dive): Kronos keeps a small tritium inventory and recycles fuel tightly — direct internal recovery over 95%, isotope separation, and accountancy — a lighter fuel plant than a D–T machine.
- [Deep Dive: The Vacuum System](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-vacuum-system-deep-dive): A fusion plasma needs an ultra-high vacuum — any stray gas would cool and contaminate it. The vacuum vessel and pumping system maintain and protect that environment.
- [Deep Dive: The Vertical Stability Problem](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/the-vertical-stability-problem-deep-dive): A strongly elongated plasma is vertically unstable and must be actively held. Kronos runs κ = 2.56 with a corrected control margin of 2.02.
- [Thermionic Energy Conversion](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/thermionic-conversion): Thermionic converters turn heat directly into electricity by boiling electrons off a hot surface — a solid-state stage in the Kronos DEC train.
- [Tokamak](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/tokamak): A tokamak confines fusion plasma in a magnetic torus. Kronos MetroVolt is a high-field, negative-triangularity spherical tokamak.
- [Tokamak vs Stellarator](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/tokamak-vs-stellarator): Tokamaks use a plasma current for higher performance but risk disruptions; stellarators are disruption-free but complex. Kronos chose the tokamak and engineers around the disruption risk.
- [Tokamaks vs Alternative Concepts](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/tokamaks-vs-alternative-concepts): Beyond tokamaks and stellarators are FRCs, spheromaks, and magnetic mirrors — each a different bet. The tokamak is the most developed, and Kronos
- [Toroidal Field Coils](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/toroidal-field-coils): The toroidal field coils produce the main confining field. In a spherical tokamak their inboard legs crowd the center stack at peak field.
- [Tritium](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/tritium): Tritium is a radioactive hydrogen isotope central to conventional D–T fusion. Kronos minimizes it, using it only for commissioning and as a ³He precursor.
- [Tritium Inventory &amp; Safety](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/tritium-inventory): Tritium is radioactive and regulated, so the on-site amount matters. Kronos
- [The Troyon Beta Limit](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/troyon-limit): The Troyon limit caps normalized beta before instability. It is the binding constraint on the Kronos design point at β_N = 4.96.
- [The Vacuum Vessel](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/vacuum-vessel): The vacuum vessel holds the ultra-high vacuum the plasma needs and forms the first safety boundary — sitting between plasma and magnets.
- [Vertical Displacement Event (VDE)](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/vertical-displacement-event): A tall, elongated plasma is vertically unstable and can drift into the wall — a VDE. Kronos holds κ = 2.56 with a control margin of 2.02.
- [Watch — Kronos Fusion Films](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/videos): Eleven short films on compact, low-neutron fusion — the physics, engineering, and economics behind Kronos MetroVolt.
- [Wall Loading &amp; Heat Flux](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/wall-loading): Wall loading is the power per unit area the first wall must handle. Kronos
- [Water Use &amp; Siting](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/water-use-and-siting): A direct-conversion, thermally-light fusion plant uses far less cooling water than a steam station — widening where it can be sited.
- [What are the main approaches to fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-are-the-main-approaches-to-fusion): The two big families are magnetic confinement (tokamaks and stellarators) and inertial confinement (lasers). Kronos is a compact, high-field magnetic tokamak.
- [What are Tier-1 and Tier-2 simulations?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-are-tier-1-and-tier-2-simulations): Kronos
- [What does 'low-neutron' mean?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-does-low-neutron-mean): Low-neutron means most of the fusion energy emerges as charged particles, not neutrons. Kronos
- [Deep Dive: What First Plasma Means](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-first-plasma-means)
- [What fuels does fusion use?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-fuels-does-fusion-use): Most fusion uses deuterium–tritium. Kronos uses low-neutron deuterium–helium-3, with deuterium from seawater and helium-3 bred in the plant itself.
- [What happens if a fusion plant loses power?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-happens-if-a-fusion-plant-loses-power): It shuts down safely on its own. A fusion plasma needs continuous input to exist, so losing power stops the reaction — the opposite of a fission decay-heat risk.
- [What happens to the helium a fusion plant makes?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-happens-to-the-helium): Fusion produces helium as its
- [What if the magnets fail?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-if-the-magnets-fail): A superconducting magnet failure (a quench) is a known, engineered-for event: detection systems safely dump the stored energy, and the plasma simply stops.
- [What Intellectual Property Does Kronos Hold?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-intellectual-property-does-kronos-hold): Kronos holds patents covering its high-field superconducting magnet technology and its two-machine breeder/burner architecture, alongside an openly published physics record. Specifics are available through the company.
- [What is a burning plasma?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-a-burning-plasma): A burning plasma is one where the energy from fusion itself provides a significant share of the heating. Kronos runs a driven burn, self-heated but sustained by external input.
- [What is a fusion pilot plant?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-a-fusion-pilot-plant): A pilot plant is a smaller machine that carries the gate-adjudication mission before a full commercial unit. The Kronos FPP is a ~0.25 GW-class device at R₀ = 2.7 m.
- [What is a fusion reactor made of?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-a-fusion-reactor-made-of): A fusion reactor is built around superconducting magnets, a refractory first wall, a vacuum vessel and shield, and — for Kronos — a direct-energy-conversion train.
- [What is a spherical tokamak?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-a-spherical-tokamak): A spherical tokamak squeezes the donut into a cored apple — a low aspect ratio that improves stability and efficiency. Kronos MetroVolt runs at aspect ratio 2.0.
- [What is a superconductor, and why does fusion need one?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-a-superconductor): A superconductor carries electricity with zero resistance. High-temperature superconductors make the strong, efficient magnets that compact fusion depends on.
- [What Is Aegis Used For?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-aegis-used-for): Aegis is the compact, fixed-site form of the Kronos burner — firm ~+850 MWe power for defense bases and forward installations, rail-delivered and assembled on a footprint of about 1.66 acres.
- [What is direct energy conversion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-direct-energy-conversion): Direct energy conversion captures the energy of charged fusion products straight as electricity, skipping the steam turbine — a defining feature of the Kronos design.
- [What Is Firm Power?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-firm-power): Firm power is electricity you can count on at any hour, regardless of weather. The Kronos machines are steady-state, so they deliver firm, dispatchable output as a structural feature — not an average.
- [What is fusion's environmental impact?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-fusions-environmental-impact): Fusion has an unusually light footprint: no CO₂, no long-lived waste, little water and land, no fuel mining — with a low-neutron design lighter still.
- [What Is Kronos Fusion Energy?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-kronos-fusion-energy): Kronos Fusion Energy is a compact fusion company building two machines: HYPERION, a spherical-tokamak D–T breeder that makes fuel, and a D–³He tandem-mirror burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) that burns it cleanly.
- [What is nuclear fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-nuclear-fusion): Nuclear fusion is the joining of light atomic nuclei to release energy — the process that powers the sun, and the basis of the Kronos generators.
- [What is plasma?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-plasma): Plasma is the fourth state of matter — a hot, ionized gas of free electrons and nuclei. It
- [What is the biggest technical risk in the Kronos design?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-is-the-biggest-technical-risk): The confinement requirement — H98 = 2.28 at the Mode-D baseline — is the single largest bet, and its nonlinear-gyrokinetic verification is the outstanding item, tested first at the G1 gate.
- [Moved](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-makes-kronos-different)
- [What would prove the Kronos design wrong?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/what-would-prove-kronos-wrong): Specific, pre-registered results would. If the G1 testbed shows negative-triangularity confinement below the required threshold, the design must be re-sized — and Kronos would publish it.
- [When will fusion actually power the grid?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/when-will-fusion-power-the-grid): Kronos advances on a gated schedule rather than a marketing date — the G1 confinement testbed is roughly four years to first plasma, with each gate retiring a specific risk.
- [Where does helium-3 come from?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/where-does-helium-3-come-from): Helium-3 is scarce on Earth. Kronos runs a staged, catalyzed D–³He cycle that breeds much of its own ³He, so the plant is not hostage to thin external supply.
- [Why compact fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-compact-fusion): High-temperature superconductors let a small, high-field machine reach reactor conditions — and smaller means cheaper, faster to build, and manufacturable at fleet scale.
- [Why deuterium instead of ordinary hydrogen?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-deuterium-instead-of-hydrogen): Ordinary hydrogen fuses far too slowly for a power plant — it takes the sun billions of years. Deuterium fuses readily at temperatures a reactor can reach.
- [Why do neutrons matter in fusion?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-do-neutrons-matter-in-fusion): Neutrons carry energy but no charge — they damage materials, activate structures, and can
- [Why does fusion energy matter?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-does-fusion-energy-matter): Fusion could supply firm, clean, abundant power — the always-on, low-carbon energy a decarbonizing world needs and doesn
- [Why Does Kronos Publish Everything?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-does-kronos-publish-everything): Kronos publishes its code, data, and open problems because a compact-fusion claim is only worth as much as its reproducibility. Two open deposits and a live simulation let anyone check the numbers.
- [Why does Kronos use helium-3 instead of tritium?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-does-kronos-use-helium-3): Helium-3 gives a low-neutron reaction whose charged products can be converted directly to electricity — and Kronos breeds its own, sidestepping the scarcity problem.
- [Why is fusion energy so hard to achieve?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-is-fusion-so-hard): Fusion requires heating fuel to over 100 million degrees and confining it well enough to produce net energy — the Lawson condition. Every fusion design is a way to meet it.
- [Why is fusion valuable for defense?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-is-fusion-valuable-for-defense): Fusion offers energy security without fuel convoys — firm, islandable, domestically-fueled power that removes a major logistical vulnerability.
- [Does Kronos Skip D–T?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-kronos-skips-dt-first): No — Kronos does the opposite. The first machine, the HYPERION breeder, burns D–T on purpose to make fuel. Kronos breeds with D–T first, then burns low-neutron D–³He in the second machine.
- [Why does Kronos use negative triangularity?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-negative-triangularity): Three load-bearing reasons: an ELM-free edge that protects the converter, H-mode-grade core confinement with an L-mode edge, and density headroom.
- [Why not just build more solar and batteries?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-not-just-use-more-solar-and-batteries): Solar and batteries are essential but can
- [Why should I believe Kronos's numbers?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-should-i-believe-kronos-numbers): Because you don
- [Why does Kronos use such a strong magnetic field?](https://www.kronosfusionenergy.com/learn/why-such-a-strong-magnetic-field): Fusion power density rises with the fourth power of magnetic field, so a very-high-field machine can be far more compact than a low-field one of equal output.
